[[331.3]] 109. DAMARIS LADY MASHAM AN LEIBNIZ

[[331.4]] Oates, 20. (31.) Oktober 1705. [105.111.]

[[331.15]] S^#'r Oates 20 October 1705.

[[331.16]] I should have no Cause to wonder if you were not unwilling to Give over a commerce

[[331.17]] which brought you so poor returns as are my Letters for Yours. Your Excuseing to me therefore

[[331.18]] your silence is very obligeing as a mark of your puting a value on my correspondence that it has

[[331.19]] no claim to: But the reason you give of your not haveing writ to me sooner has renew'd in me a

[[331.20]] Sorrow which I could not but pertake in with all the world to whom were known (thō but by

[[331.21]] Fame onely) the Great Endowments and Accomplishments of that Admirable Princess whose

[[331.22]] Death has so much Afflicted you. One cannot have a deeper sense than I have of Your

[[331.23]] Particular Loss in this Universal One: and if ever Greif was just yours must be allow'd to be so.

[[331.24]] The Experience of the Wisest dos I find on some occasions attest to this truth, that La

[[331.25]] Sensibilité ne depend pas du Raisonnement. There is however much difference betwixt

[[331.26]] Them and Others; in that if Theire Reason dos not always Triumph, it yet at least hinders

[[332.1]] Passion from doing so: and it is a Happy distinction not to be Led Captive by those Tyrants

[[332.2]] under which the Generalitie of Mankind suffer a worse Slaverie than the most Arbitrarie

[[332.3]] Masters can inflict.

[[332.4]] I was Highly Honour'd in haveing any Thoughts of Mine Communicated to the Queene of

[[332.5]] Prussia: but what you thought worth the answering I cannot wonder that She vouchsaf'd a

[[332.6]] Heareing to.

[[332.7]] I have flatter'd myself since my last to you that, possibly, within another yeare I might

[[332.8]] have the oportunitie to converse with you better than by letters, in seeing You at Hanover: for if

[[332.9]] some whose Judgments I rely upon, had thought it fit for a Young Gentleman destin'd to the

[[332.10]] Study of the Law to spend a little Time first in Travelling, I should with his Fathers leave,

[[332.11]] Gladly have accompany'd my Son in such a Voyage: both as proposing great Pleasure therein;

[[332.12]] and also as haveing been persuaded that Travelling would contribute to my Health, which has

[[332.13]] been much disorder'd this Last Yeare.

[[332.14]] You have added to the many Reasons I have to Regret the Death of M^#'r Locke in leting me

[[332.15]] know that it will hinder the Publick from Profiting by your Remarks upon his Essay. The

[[332.16]] debates of Those who equally search Truth cannot but be advantageous to the discoverie of it,

[[332.17]] or to the seting it in a Clearer Light: and which ever it be, both Parties in such cases will think

[[332.18]] themselves alike Gainers.

[[332.19]] I am sorry with you that the strength or weakness of any notion which you beleeve

[[332.20]] important to be known, should not be so. It were to be wish'd that All who in respect of any

[[332.21]] Usefull Truth, have views beyond others would not neglect to communicate them, that so They

[[332.22]] may be out of danger of being useless to the World. This should methinks induce You to oblige,

[[332.23]] as M^#'r Le Clerc tells you you would do, all the Lovers of Philosophy, in explaining at Large

[[332.24]] Your Systeme; whereby it being set in a just Light, the advantages of it may neither be Lost; nor

[[332.25]] prejudic'd, by the unskilfull representation that, it may be, some other Person who shall less

[[332.26]] perfectly comprehend it, may some time, or other, venture to give of it. This I cannot but wish;

[[332.27]] and This I find some hope you will be Excited to by M^#'r Bayle's Reflection upon Your

[[332.28]] sentiments amongst Those of Others.

[[333.1]] If you have read what has been writ betwixt him and M^#'r Le Clerc on the subject of the

[[333.2]] Hypothesis of the Plastick Nature as asserted by my Father, I should be very glad to know

[[333.3]] whether what M^#'r Bayle has offer'd dos amount to any thing more than a beging of the Question

[[333.4]] That God cannot make an unknowing Agent so as to Act to wise Ends; yet without such his

[[333.5]] Perpetual direction thereof as the Cartesian Hypothesis gives to Material Causes: for if it be

[[333.6]] conceivable for God to do so, but not conceivable for senseless Matter of it self to Act for Ends;

[[333.7]] My Fathers Hypothesis is methinks sufficiently secur'd from the Retorsion of Atheists,

[[333.8]] without being in the same Case with any one which makes God the immediate Efficient

[[333.9]] Cause of all the Effects of Nature. Since my Father dos not therein assert (as M^#'r Bayle says he

[[333.10]] dos) That God has been able to give to Creatures a Facultie of Produceing Excellent

[[333.11]] Works, (viz such as is the Organization of Plants and Animals) seperate

[[333.12]] from all Knowledge etc: but Onely a Facultie of Executeing instrumentally his Ideas or

[[333.13]] Designs in the Production of such Excellent Works: so that ( according to him) there is

[[333.14]] (differently from what M^#'r Bayle asserts of his Hypothesis) an inseparable union betwixt

[[333.15]] the Power of produceing Excellent Works, and the Idea of theire Essence, and

[[333.16]] manner of produceing them. and it seems to me that there can be no Pretence for the

[[333.17]] Retorsion of Atheists unless it were asserted, That God had been able to give to Creatures a

[[333.18]] Facultie of produceing excellent works, the Ideas whereof never were in any Understanding:

[[333.19]] But my Father is so far from asserting any such thing as This, that he holds the Operations of

[[333.20]] the Plastick Nature to be essentially and necessarilie dependent on the Ideas in the

[[333.21]] divine Intellect. So that (I conceive) if Matter could be suppos'd to have of it self that same

[[333.22]] Pow'r which Plastick Natures are said to have by the Gift of God, it would not help

[[334.1]] the Atheists Cause at all: Because the Pow'r giv'n to Plastick Natures being onely a Pow'r to

[[334.2]] Execute the Ideas of a Perfect Mind; if there were no Mind in the Universe; this Pow'r in the

[[334.3]] Matter must Lye for ever Dormant, and unproductive of any such Excellent Work as is spoken

[[334.4]] of.

[[334.5]] Thus I see not in my Fathers Hypothesis that there is Effectively (as M^#'r Bayle affirms) a

[[334.6]] Compatibilitie suppos'd of a Pow'r to Organize Animals, with the want of

[[334.7]] Knowledge. Since to the Production of such a work as This, two things (according to my

[[334.8]] Father) must concur viz the Idea of the work to be Executed, with an Executive Pow'r of

[[334.9]] bringing this Idea into real Existence: and it is onely the last of these which he ascribes to

[[334.10]] Plastick Natures.

[[334.11]] But M^#'r Bayle argues, That if Plastick Natures have no Intire Efficiencie of theire owne,

[[334.12]] they will then need such Perpetual direction as is ascrib'd to Material Causes; and so my

[[334.13]] Fathers Hypothesis will be but in the same Case with the Cartesian. M^#'r Bayle

[[334.14]] Affirms this; but (as I think) he no where Proves it: All that he offers amounting (as I have

[[334.15]] alreadie observ'd) onelie to a beging of this Question, that God cannot make a Creature to Act

[[334.16]] but either from Ideas of what it dos; or else by such Perpetual Direction as that of the

[[334.17]] Cartesian Material Causes. Whence he rigthly infers that if Plastick Natures Act not by Ideas

[[334.18]] which They have, as it is presum'd the Destroying Angel did to in distinguishing the

[[334.19]] Egyptians from the Israelites etc. They then must Act as He supposes Fire, had it so

[[334.20]] pleas'd God, might have done, in Destroying the First Born of Egypt; Viz by Gods Perpetual

[[334.21]] applying and directing it.

[[334.22]] But to Any ones bare Assertion that a thing is Inconceivable, it is surely answer sufficient

[[334.23]] that Others find it not to be so. Thō my Father has giv'n some instances which he thinks prove

[[334.24]] the Possibilitie of such a manner of Action as he ascribes to Plastick Natures; Viz in the

[[334.25]] Operations of Habits: as (for Example) Those of Singing and Danceing, which shall oftentimes

[[334.26]] direct the Motions of the Body, or Voice, without any Consideration of what the next

[[334.27]] Note, or Motion should be.

[[334.28]] I beg Leave here to tresspass so much farther on Your Patience, as to observe to you one

[[334.29]] thing wherin M^#'r Bayle is mistaken in reference to this matter, which has not been taken notice

[[334.30]] of, and that is, in a presumeing that my Father design'd in introduceing his Hypothesis, to

[[334.31]] oppose the Modern Cartesians: whereas He (not understanding French) did not know that the

[[334.32]] Modern Cartesians differ'd so much from theire Master as to hold that God was the Immediate

[[334.33]] Efficient Cause of all the Effects of Nature and the Hypothesis of the Plastick Nature (produc'd

[[335.1]] by him for the acquiting from the suspicion of Atheism some who held a Plastick Life distinct

[[335.2]] from the Animal) was very far from haveing the Cartesians in View; however They may find

[[335.3]] themselves convinc'd when the opinion of such is condemn'd as held that God himself did All

[[335.4]] immediately in the Efformation and organization of the Bodies of Animals, as well as the

[[335.5]] other phenomena: which with the Opinion of all things comeing to pass Fortuitously, my Father

[[335.6]] consider'd as the onely two Hypothesises which were oppos'd to that of Plastick Natures.

[[335.7]] Now M^#'r Bayle considering Perpetual Direction onelie in such a sense as makes God

[[335.8]] the Immediate Efficient cause of all the Effects of Nature, presumes that my Father is oblig'd to

[[335.9]] deny all kind of Perpetual Direction to Plastick Natures; which (as I take it) he dos not: Since

[[335.10]] (according to him) theire Operations are always determin'd by the Ideas in the Divine Intellect;

[[335.11]] and his Hypothesis opposes onely such Direction as makes God the Immediate Efficient Cause

[[335.12]] of all the Works of Nature. Plastick Natures being by him substituted as the Agents or

[[335.13]] Executioners of the Divine Will and Pleasure. As Perpetual Direction then is understood, or

[[335.14]] may be Explain'd, it seemes to me that Plastick Natures may be, and are by my Father, in what

[[335.15]] he says of them, both affirm'd and deny'd to have Perpetual Direction: in which, if he talks

[[335.16]] Contradictiously, or Inconsistently it lies upon M^#'r Bayle to show that he dos so, Stateing first

[[335.17]] rightly what is herein asserted by him.

[[335.18]] I pretend not at all to be Positive in any thing which I have here ventur'd to say on so nice

[[335.19]] a subject, and so much above my Examination as not easilie to be set in a due Light by two so

[[335.20]] Acute and extraordinarie Men as both M^#'r Le Clerc and M^#'r Bayle are. I onelie take the libertie

[[335.21]] briefly to suggest to you my Thoughts thereon to the end that I may learn from you how far they

[[335.22]] are Right.

[[335.23]] The Last answer of M^#'r Le Clerc I have not yet read, his Civilitie in sending me one (which

[[335.24]] I heare has miscarry'd) haveing made me thus Long neglect buying it. But I am told that M^#'r

[[335.25]] Bayle will still reply: and that the subject of the Controversie is by some thought to be by M^#'r Le

[[335.26]] Clercs answer too much enlarg'd in a Consideration of the usefulness of the Hypothesis of

[[335.27]] Plastick Natures, which is not necessarie to the inquirie, whether, or no, this Hypothesis is

[[335.28]] expos'd to the Retorsion of Atheists.

[[335.29]] On which subject I have dwelt Long enough both to need your Pardon, and to forbid my

[[335.30]] adding any thing More to this Letter that might induce you to explain to me farther your

[[335.31]] Sentiments on some other important Inquiries mention'd in the last letter you Honourd me with.

[[336.1]] I am with due acknowledgment of your Condescention in incourageing me in this Manner

[[336.2]] to trouble you, and with very great Esteem and Respect

[[336.3]] S^#'r Your Most Humble Servant Da Masham

[[336.4]] Your last letter to me lay several weeks in this country before it came to my Hands as

[[336.5]] being sent to a Gentlemans house where I was dayly exspected. All acidents of this nature will

[[336.6]] be prevented and M^#'r Pickelaer have no farther trouble than to send them to the Post House if

[[336.7]] you please to direct thus

[[336.8]] For My Lady Masham at Oates.

[[336.9]] To be left with M^#'r Harison at the Crowne in Harlow.
